Scope: Selected source/input/IL identities, exact mapped scopes, alias preservation and physical caller edges; no application or runtime test

ReviewedReplacements.Reason: Checks the input enumerable and snapshots it to a List before calling the ICollection overload; the overloads have distinct signatures and need no numeric suffix.
Validates a nonnull source and returns the negation of Enumerable.Any.
Validates the source then returns the negation of Enumerable.Any with the predicate; LINQ validates the predicate.
Returns true for null, otherwise invokes the empty-sequence predicate.
Returns true for null without inspecting the predicate; otherwise tests that no item matches.
Returns default(T) for zero or multiple items, including zero for non-nullable value types; exactly one item is fetched by enumerating source again.
Assigns FirstOrDefault(predicate), boxes it and tests against null. A missing non-nullable value-type match therefore still returns true.
Returns Array.Empty<T> for a null value and a new one-element array otherwise.
Materializes a new List and wraps it read-only; it is a copied snapshot rather than a live view over the input.
Initially replaces target contents if sequences differ, then returns a disposable Rx subscription that casts source items to the target type and applies collection changes.

BehaviorLimits: SyncFrom uses set difference, so it does not establish ordering or reconcile duplicate multiplicities.
ICollection add/remove overloads enumerate inputs directly; IEnumerable overloads snapshot first. Clear-then-add can empty self-aliased input.
SingleOrNull returns default(T) for zero/multiple items, and enumerates again for the single item; only the prior inferred 6.3 alias changes.
FirstOrDefault followed by boxing/non-null testing can report true for missing non-nullable value-type matches. Archive publishing uses a reference-type instantiation.
Partition/generator input validation occurs on first MoveNext. Partition owns and disposes its source enumerator; re-enumeration can reuse an untouched iterator only on its original thread.
Mirroring Add/Replace operate by value without preserving event indices; Replace adds new values before removing old ones. Other actions reset from Sender.
Recent-item handling trims exactly one last value only when adding a missing item; moving an existing item does not trim. Installation uses a limit of 42.
TryPop catches all exceptions inside its Count/Pop try and is not atomic for concurrent callers.
Archive publishing removes one existing related-GUID entry, adds the new info, updates counts and emits Created followed by optional Locked; public contracts remain unchanged.
Explicit iterator MoveNext local aliases remain outside the current scope guard; their runtime method names/contracts were preserved. No unsupported guards were bypassed.
